caption: The frame buffer holds all 786,432 pixels of the 1024 × 768 screen at 3 bytes each, so 2,359,296 bytes or 2.25 MiB. The video controller re-reads that whole buffer 60 times a second — 141.6 MB/s — and sends the rows to the monitor, which is why the picture does not fade.

spec.title: Raster scan path
spec.aria: A five-block chain from CPU through display processor to a frame buffer holding 2,359,296 bytes, then a video controller that reads the buffer 60 times a second at 141.6 MB/s and drives a 1024 by 768 monitor.
